validity.recommendation: none - existence, classification, and non-duplicate status all confirmed
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed by an independent SEC filing. Regency Energy Partners LP's FY2005 Form 10-K (sec.gov, filed 2006) names the 'Regency Intrastate Enhancement Project' explicitly, gives planning start Jan 2005, construction start May 2005, completion Dec 2005, cost $157.0 million, and describes the physical scope in three phases: (1) an 8-mile, 12-inch Dubach lateral completed July 2005 (NOT part of this GEM segment's own diameter/length scope - see spec note below), (2) a 40-mile, 24-inch system loop completed Oct 2005 (+100 MMcf/d), (3) an 80-mile, 30-inch 'Winnsboro extension' completed Dec 2005, raising total system capacity from 200 to 800 MMcf/d. A second, fully independent federal document - a FERC Final EIS for an unrelated project ('East Texas To Mississippi Expansion Project', FERC, May 2007, viewed via Google Books) - separately references 'Regency Pipeline...an 80-mile long, 30-inch-diameter intrastate natural gas pipeline' and 'Regency Intrastate Gas...recently completed construction...currently in the final phase of construction' in a cumulative-impacts context, corroborating the same 80-mile/30-inch/Louisiana facts from a wholly separate regulatory proceeding. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission is correct - the 10-K frames RIGS as its 'Transportation' segment (as opposed to its separately-described 'Gathering and Processing' systems), and the FERC EIS independently calls it an 'intrastate natural gas pipeline', not a gathering line. DUPLICATE CHECK (vs P0244, same pipeline name on the roster): NOT a duplicate. P0244 is the original 1974-1989 base system (200 mi, 200 MMcf/d, diameters 12/16/20/24in per the 10-K's itemized asset list: Elm Grove 12in, North Louisiana Pipeline 12in+16in, Panda 20in+24in). P5823 is the distinct 2005 capital project that expanded that same base system - this is GEM's standard base-system/expansion-phase pairing (same convention endorsed for the Florida Gas Transmission cluster in this batch), not a double-count. The Capacity value on this row (600 MMcf/d) is the project's ADDED capacity (800 post-project minus 200 pre-project = 600), not a restated system total, so it does not trip the aggregate-vs-segment rule either. Opened and read to exhaustion: the SEC 10-K (full text) and the FERC EIS Google Books snippet; other harvested citations on this row are covered individually below and in fills[].

validity.recommendation: correct Diameter from '30, 42' to '24, 30' - add the documented 24in phase, drop the unconfirmed 42in figure pending a segment-specific source
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Diameter='30, 42' does not match what the primary source actually documents for this project. The SEC 10-K itemizes the Enhancement Project's two in-scope phases (the 8-mile/12in Dubach lateral is described elsewhere in the same 10-K as excluded from this segment's own length/diameter list, consistent with GEM's own wiki page which also lists only 24/30/42in, never 12in, for this row) as a 40-mile, 24-inch system loop and an 80-mile, 30-inch Winnsboro extension - i.e. 24in and 30in, with NO mention of 42-inch pipe anywhere in the full 10-K text (I searched the complete document for '42-inch'/'42 inch' - every '42' hit was a page number or unrelated financial figure). The gem.wiki page's footnote for 42in traces to offshore-technology.com's marketdata page (GlobalData), which I verified live via a Wayback capture: it describes the pipeline as a SYSTEM-WIDE '724km-long...maximum diameter of 42 inches' - a system total (724km = ~450mi) that does not match GEM's own combined P0244+P5823 total of 320mi either, meaning this aggregator's figures are themselves internally inconsistent with GEM's tracked segments and cannot be trusted as segment-specific corroboration for 42in on THIS row. Recommend replacing '30, 42' with '24, 30', both independently documented for this specific project by the SEC 10-K.

validity.recommendation: add 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.' as the specific Operator entity; have a researcher verify current Owner1 percentage against the documented JV history before treating 'ETP Legacy 100%' as final
validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline's actual operating/reporting entity, per Energy Transfer's own current operations page (energytransfer.com/ops_intrastate.aspx, verified live) is 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.' ('RIGS is a 450-mile intrastate pipeline...2.1 Bcf/d'), corroborated independently by two SEC EDGAR filings across different years: a 2011-filed audited financial statement exhibit titled 'Audited Financial Statement of RIGS Haynesville Partnership' (Regency Energy Partners LP 10-K, FY2010) and full-text-search hits for the same entity name across ~60 other EDGAR documents. That 2010 audited-financials exhibit also states that the pipeline was reorganized in 2009 from a predecessor 'Regency Intrastate Gas LLC' into 'RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.', a JOINT VENTURE - Regency held only 43% (Sept 2009) rising to 49.99% (April 2010) via purchases from a partner, 'EFS Haynesville, LLC' - i.e. NOT a wholly Regency/ETP-owned asset at that time. GEM's current Owner1='ETP Legacy' at 100% may reflect a later full buyout, but I could not independently confirm the date or mechanism of reaching 100%, only that a genuine JV history exists that a single 'ETP Legacy 100%' line does not capture. Separately, 'ETP Legacy' IS a real term Energy Transfer uses in its own SEC 10-Ks (confirmed via EDGAR full-text search, 6 hits 2013-2019, referring to pre-Sunoco-merger legacy-ETP asset/unit classes) so the label itself is not fabricated - it's plausible but unverified for this specific 100% claim on this specific row. Recommend a researcher check Energy Transfer's current 10-K subsidiary schedule for RIGS Haynesville Partnership Co.'s present ownership split before relying on 100%.

summary: P5823 (Regency Intrastate Enhancement Project) is real, correctly classified as transmission, and correctly kept as a separate row from base-system P0244 (not a duplicate); sourced 12 of 15 owed cells (SEC 10-K + independent FERC EIS via Google Books + current operator site + SEC-filed JV financials + Wikipedia), left Pressure/StartLocation/StartPrefecture UNRESOLVED, and flagged two concerns: Diameter should be corrected from '30, 42' to '24, 30' (42in is sourced only to an internally-inconsistent system-wide aggregator page), and Owner1='ETP Legacy' 100% should be checked against a documented 2009-2010 joint-venture ownership structure (43-49.99% Regency stake) before treating it as final; also surfaced a likely undocumented later expansion of the RIGS system (routed to P0244 as a cross-row lead).
